word_sets.name: Set 4 · Conceding and concluding
words: لا بدّ من الاعتراف بأن / من المسلَّم به
في حين أنه من الصحيح أن
مع أخذ كل شيء بعين الاعتبار

sentences: It is often claimed that social media brings people together.
كثيرًا ما يُزعَم أن وسائل التواصل الاجتماعي تقرّب بين الناس.
I see your point, but I'm afraid I can't agree.
أفهم وجهة نظرك، لكن يؤسفني أنني لا أستطيع الموافقة.
Admittedly, school uniforms are not cheap; even so, they reduce pressure on students.
لا بدّ من الاعتراف بأن الزيّ المدرسي ليس رخيصًا؛ ومع ذلك فهو يقلّل الضغط على الطلاب.
While it is true that cars are convenient, they are also a major cause of pollution in Cairo.
في حين أنه من الصحيح أن السيارات مريحة، فهي أيضًا سبب رئيسي للتلوّث في القاهرة.
Opponents argue that homework puts too much pressure on young children.
يرى المعارضون أن الواجبات المنزلية تضع ضغطًا كبيرًا على الأطفال الصغار.
With all due respect, there is no evidence to support that claim.
مع كامل احترامي، لا يوجد دليل يدعم هذا الادعاء.
On balance, I believe the advantages outweigh the disadvantages.
إجمالًا، أعتقد أن المزايا تفوق العيوب.
This brings me to my final point.
وهذا يقودني إلى نقطتي الأخيرة.
Not only is the plan expensive, but it is also unlikely to work.
ليست الخطة مكلفة فحسب، بل من غير المحتمل أيضًا أن تنجح.
What really matters is not who wins the debate, but what we learn from it.
ما يهمّ حقًا ليس من يفوز بالمناظرة، بل ما نتعلّمه منها.

grammar.intro_en: A strong argument has a clear structure: introduction (background + your position) → body paragraphs (one main idea each: topic sentence, explanation, example or evidence) → counter-argument + rebuttal → conclusion (summary + final thought). This week you use the grammar of the whole level inside this structure.
grammar.intro_ar: كثير من المتعلمين يكتبون المقال كفقرة واحدة طويلة، أو يكرّرون رأيهم دون دليل، أو يتجاهلون الرأي الآخر. المقال والعرض الجيّدان لهما هيكل واضح: مقدمة تعرض الموضوع ورأيك، ثم فقرة لكل فكرة تبدأ بجملة رئيسية (topic sentence) ثم شرح ثم مثال أو دليل، ثم تعرض الرأي المخالف وتردّ عليه (Admittedly… Even so…)، ثم خاتمة تلخّص ولا تضيف أفكارًا جديدة. واستخدم قواعد هذا المستوى لتقوية أسلوبك: المبني للمجهول غير الشخصي، والجمل المؤكِّدة (cleft)، والقلب (inversion)، وأدوات التخفيف (hedging).

rows: It is often claimed that… · This essay will argue that… · In this talk I'd like to…
impersonal passive: It is widely believed that…
First and foremost… · Furthermore… · A case in point is… · Let me illustrate this with…
cleft: What matters most is… · participle clause: Having considered…
Opponents argue that… · Admittedly… · While it is true that…
hedging: It could be argued that… · may · tend to
Even so… · However, this ignores… · There is little evidence that…
inversion: Not only… but also… · Rarely do…
On balance… · All things considered… · To sum up… · I'd like to finish by…
probability: … is bound to / likely to…

notes: One paragraph = one main idea. Start each body paragraph with a clear topic sentence.
Support every claim with a reason AND an example or a fact.
In a presentation, use signposts (Moving on to… · This brings me to…) so the audience always knows where you are.
Never introduce a new argument in the conclusion.

exercises.title: Exercise 1 · Which part of an essay is each sentence from? Write Introduction, Main point, Counter-argument, Rebuttal or Conclusion.
exercises.instructions: Which part of an essay is each sentence from? Write Introduction, Main point, Counter-argument, Rebuttal or Conclusion.
items: 1) Opponents argue that uniforms limit students' creativity.
2) All things considered, I am convinced that uniforms do more good than harm.
3) It is often claimed that school uniforms are old-fashioned, but this essay will argue that they are still useful.
4) First and foremost, uniforms reduce the pressure to wear expensive clothes.
5) Even so, students can still express their personality through their ideas, hobbies and work.

3) ___, the course is expensive, but it is worth every pound.
4) “Exercise is the best medicine.” — “___! I feel better every time I go running.”

exercises.title: Exercise 3 · Rewrite the sentences with a Level 5 structure, using the words in brackets.
exercises.instructions: Rewrite the sentences with a Level 5 structure, using the words in brackets.
items: 1) People say that debating improves critical thinking. (It)
2) I have never heard such a convincing argument. (Never)
3) We need more evidence. (What)
4) Young people usually trust online sources too easily. (tend)
5) The government will almost certainly change the law. (bound)
6) After she had listened to both sides, she changed her mind. (Having)
answers: 1) It is said that debating improves critical thinking.
2) Never have I heard such a convincing argument.
3) What we need is more evidence.
4) Young people tend to trust online sources too easily.
5) The government is bound to change the law.
6) Having listened to both sides, she changed her mind.

2) لا بدّ من الاعتراف بأن هذا الحل مكلف.
3) مع أخذ كل شيء بعين الاعتبار، يجب أن تكون الواجبات المنزلية اختيارية.

answers: 1) I see / understand your point, but I beg to differ.
3) All things considered, homework should be optional.
4) It is worth noting that most students support this decision.

write_speak: Write & Speak — Write a for-and-against essay (220–250 words): “Should university education be completely free?” Present both sides, answer the counter-argument and give your conclusion. Use grammar from at least five different weeks of this level. Then turn it into a 3-minute debate speech and record it.
other:
Example: Should university education be completely free?
It is often claimed that education is a right, not a privilege. Many people therefore believe that university should be completely free for every student. This essay will examine both sides before reaching a conclusion.
First and foremost, free university education gives talented students from poor families the same opportunities as wealthy ones. A case in point is my cousin from a village near Minya, who became a doctor only because she did not have to pay tuition fees. Not only did free education change her life, but it also benefited her whole community, where she now works.
Furthermore, a country with more graduates is likely to have a stronger economy. Educated workers tend to earn more, pay more tax and start more businesses.
Opponents argue, however, that free education is extremely expensive for the state. Admittedly, the money has to come from somewhere, and overcrowded lecture halls with three hundred students can lower the quality of teaching. It could also be argued that students value their studies less when they pay nothing.
Even so, these problems are not a reason to charge everyone. What is needed is better investment and smarter spending, such as linking free places to good grades and offering loans to those who can afford to repay them later.
On balance, I believe that university education should remain free, provided that the government invests enough to keep standards high. After all, a nation's future is bound to depend on the quality of its graduates.
